audio_narrative_it.text: Il top policymaker dell'ECB ha avvertito che i prezzi elevati del petrolio potrebbero spingere la BCE a inasprire ulteriormente i tassi; ciò potrebbe pesare sull'apertura di lunedì, con gli investitori cauti sul mercato euro. Parallelamente, la persistenza dell'inflazione negli USA sta esercitando pressione sulla Fed, il che potrebbe far aumentare i rendimenti obbligazionari e frenare l'appetito per il rischio, influenzando negativamente l'S&P 500. Infine, la ripresa della domanda cinese di petrolio, in risposta alle tensioni nello Stretto di Hormuz, potrebbe sostenere i prezzi energetici, mantenendo il Brent sotto pressione e rafforzando il dollaro, con possibili ripercussioni sui mercati emergenti lunedì.

audio_narrative_en.title: Opening
audio_narrative_en.text: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The markets are observing the weekend pause; we’ll return on Monday with fresh data.

audio_narrative_en.title: Market Closes
audio_narrative_en.text: In Friday’s session the S&P 500 closed at 7,096 points, up 0.86%. The VIX fell to 15.84, down 11.21%. The Dollar Index (DXY) stayed essentially flat at 99.12, up 0.03%. Gold touched $4,336 per ounce, stable with a 0.04% increase. Brent fell to $114.61, down 2.81%. The STOXX 600 closed at 63.49, down 0.81%. The FTSE MIB rose to 52,515, up 1.36%. The Nikkei closed at 64,411, down 1.93%. Shanghai fell to 3,088.11, down 1.18%. The Hang Seng closed at 24,086, down 0.60%. U.S. 10‑year Treasury yields rose to 4.97%, up 0.63%. The 10‑year BTP stayed at 3.73%.

audio_narrative_en.title: News and Outlook
audio_narrative_en.text: The ECB’s top policymaker warned that high oil prices could push the ECB to tighten rates further; this could weigh on Monday’s opening, with investors cautious in the euro market. Meanwhile, persistent inflation in the U.S. is putting pressure on the Fed, which could raise bond yields and dampen risk appetite, negatively impacting the S&P 500. Finally, a rebound in Chinese oil demand in response to tensions in the Strait of Hormuz could support energy prices, keep Brent under pressure, and strengthen the dollar, with possible repercussions for emerging markets on Monday.

audio_narrative_en.title: Macroeconomics
audio_narrative_en.text: No macroeconomic releases are scheduled over the weekend; the macro agenda will resume on Monday with U.S. CPI and the European PMI index.
